description: Eager: Exploring Machine Learning and Particle Image Velocimetry to Elucidate the Role of Geomorphic Complexity in Enhancing Damage during Extreme Wind Events in Puerto Rico is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Forrest Masters, University of Florida (ufl.edu). This dataset was generated during an experiment that investigated topographic wind speedup effects on the island of Puerto Rico. In the aftermath of Hurricane Maria (2017) the mountainous regions were severely affected by structural damages caused by wind speedup. Coverage: test. DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: wind speedup, complex topography, PIV, complex terrain, boundary layer wind tunnel, machine learning. Published 2022-11-30. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
